Начинай задачу: Создать приложение-читалку для детей с текстами на трёх уровнях владения языком: A1, A2, B1. Нужно: продумать структуру приложения (список текстов, выбор уровня, режим чтения), подобрать или составить короткие адаптированные истории для каждого уровня с учётом возрастной аудитории, оформить интерфейс простым и понятным для детей, добавить возможность переключения уровней. Формат — веб-страница, которую можно открыть в браузере (или уточнить у пользователя). Тексты подобрать готовые короткие истории по уровням, если пользователь не даст своих. Ранее задача вставала на старте — нужно довести до готового результата.

(ранние шаги убраны из памяти — главное перенесено в блокнот задачи, подробности — в журнале)

Часть 2 A2.6 (append).

Ben read the first page. \"May 3, 1975,\" he read. \"Today was a good day. I rode my bicycle to school. I saw my friends. We played in the park. We climbed the old oak tree. It is the best tree in the world. I love my town.\" Ben turned the page. \"May 10, 1975,\" he read. \"Today, my mother made a cake. It was chocolate. It was delicious. I ate two pieces. My father laughed. He said I would get a stomachache. I did not. I was fine.\" Ben turned another page. \"May 17, 1975,\" he read. \"Today, it rained. I could not play outside. I stayed at home. I read a book. It was about a girl who went on an adventure. I want to go on an adventure too. Maybe one day, I will.\" The children listened. They felt like they knew Mary. \"She is like us,\" said Zoe. \"She likes to play. She likes cake. She likes books.\" \"Yes,\" said Lily. \"People in the past are not so different from us.\" \"But their life is different,\" said Max. \"No computers. No phones. No video games.\" \"But they had fun too,\" said Ben. \"They played outside. They climbed trees. They rode bicycles.\" The children thought about this. They looked at the diary again. It was blue. \"This is a beautiful ribbon,\" said Zoe. \"Maybe Mary wore it in her hair.\" The children looked at the ribbon. \"Or maybe she used it for something else,\" said Max. \"Maybe she tied it around a gift.\" \"Or maybe she won it in a race,\" said Ben. The children did not know. But they liked the ribbon. \"We should keep these things safe,\" said Lily. \"They are from the past. I hope she writes to me.\" The children were quiet. \"It is sad when friends move away,\" said Lily. \"Yes,\" said Zoe. \"But they promised to write letters.\" \"Letters are special,\" said Ben. \"People do not write letters much now. We had a big picnic. We saw fireworks. They were beautiful. I love fireworks. They light up the sky.\" The children smiled. \"We also see fireworks on Independence Day,\" said Zoe. \"Yes,\" said Max. \"Some things do not change.\" The children felt happy. "We could keep it," said Lily. "We could show it to our families." "We could take it to a museum," said Ben. "People there would like it." "But Mary asked us to write a letter back," said Zoe. "She wanted us to put a new letter in the box and bury it again." The children thought. "Mary wanted someone in the future to find her letter," said Max. "We found it. Now we should do the same thing." "Yes," said Lily. "We should write a letter to the future. We should put it in the box. We should bury it again." "That is a great idea," said Ben. "But we should also show the things to our families first," said Zoe. "They would love to see them." "Yes," said Max. "We can show them today. Then tomorrow, we can write our letter and bury the box again." The children agreed. They were excited. They were going to be part of history. They were going to send a message to the future.`, choices:[{t:'Показать вещи семьям',n:'s9'},{t:'Сразу написать письмо в будущее',n:'s10'}]},
 s8:{text:`Ben read the last pages of the diary. "August 20, 1975," he read. "Today, I put my things in a box. I wrote a letter. I put the letter in the box. I am going to bury the box under the old oak tree in the park. I want someone in the future to find it. I want them to know about my life. I want them to know that I was here. I hope they are happy. I hope the world is a good place. Goodbye, friend from the future. With love, Mary." Ben closed the diary. The children were quiet. They felt something special. They had read Mary's message. They had connected with a girl from 1975. "She was brave," said Zoe. "She put her things in a box and buried them. She did not know if anyone would find them." "But we found them," said Max. "We found her message." "And we should answer it," said Lily. "We should write a letter to the future. We should put it in the box. We should bury it again." "Yes," said Ben. "We should do what Mary did." The children agreed. They were going to write a letter to the future. They were going to be part of history.`, choices:[{t:'Написать письмо в будущее',n:'s10'}]},
 s9:{text:`The children took the time capsule home. They showed it to their families. Their families were amazed. "This is from 1975!" said Max's father. "I was a child then!" "Look at the coin," said Lily's mother. "I remember coins like this." "And the ribbon," said Zoe's grandmother. "I had a ribbon like this when I was a girl." The children were happy. Their families loved the time capsule. They told stories about 1975. They talked about the music, the clothes, and the games. The children listened. They learned a lot. "People in 1975 had fun too," said Max. "Yes," said Lily. "They just had fun in different ways." The next day, the children met in the park. They had paper and a pen. They wanted to write a letter to the future. They wanted to tell people in the future about their lives. They wanted to be like Mary.`, choices:[{t:'Написать письмо в будущее',n:'s10'}]},
 s10:{text:`The children sat under the old oak tree. They had paper and a pen. They wanted to write a letter to the future. "What should we write?" asked Max. "We should tell them about our lives," said Lily. "Like Mary did." "Yes," said Ben. "We should tell them about our town. About our school. About our games." "And about our dreams," said Zoe. The children thought. Then they started to write. "Dear friend from the future," they wrote. "We are Max, Lily, Ben, and Zoe. We are ten years old. We found Mary's time capsule under the old oak tree. We read her letter. We read her diary. We looked at her photo. We felt like we knew her. We want you to know about our lives. We live in the same town. We go to the same school. We play in the same park. We love to play video games. We love to watch movies. We love to read books. Our favorite food is pizza. Our favorite color is blue, like Mary's. We hope you are happy in the future. We hope the world is a good place. Please write a letter back and put it in this box. Then bury it again. Someone in the future will find it. With love, Max, Lily, Ben, and Zoe." The children put the letter in the box. They closed it. They locked it. They buried it under the old oak tree. They stood up. They looked at each other. They smiled. "We did it," said Max. "We are part of history now," said Lily. "Someone in the future will find our letter," said Ben. "And they will know about us," said Zoe. The children walked home. They felt happy. They had done something special. They had sent a message to the future. And under the old oak tree, the time capsule waited. It waited for someone else to find it. It waited for a new friend from the future.`, ending:true},
